head_semantics.note: The receipt commit necessarily lands one commit after the snapshot it approves. This records both and enumerates the difference instead of claiming they are the same.

phase_repro.why: LoRA dropout is 0.1 and select_trainer.py:535 calls model.train() before selection, so stochastic dropout masks are active while per-sample target gradients are taken. Non-reproducible target gradients would make every downstream selection hash meaningless, so this is checked, not assumed.
phase_repro.VERDICT: Target gradients are NOT bit-reproducible, but the cause is floating-point non-determinism, not active dropout: 54/64 rows identical, perturbed rows at ~1e-4, row cosine >=0.99992. Downstream impact is 1 of 2707 selected examples (DSMC Jaccard 0.999261). REPORTED FOR DECISION, not silently resolved: no eval mode was set, no dropout forced to 0, no seed changed, and neither cache was picked. Both caches are retained with hashes.

structure.interpretation: NOT dropout. LoRA dropout p=0.1 would apply an independent random mask per sample, so ALL 64 rows would differ and row cosine would fall well below 0.99. Observed: 54/64 rows are BIT-IDENTICAL, and the 10 that differ are perturbed densely (91% of elements) but only at ~1e-4 on unit-norm vectors (row cosine >= 0.99992, relative mean diff 1.4e-3). That is the signature of bf16/GPU reduction-order non-determinism in the 8-way distributed backward, not of stochastic dropout masks.
